reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Safety requirements for most capable models
themes.definition: Proposals for common safety requirements for frontier AI models, including pre-release testing and reporting of serious safety failures, and capacity to assess capable systems.
themes.inclusion: Passages calling for testing, safety standards or incident reporting for the most capable AI models.
themes.boundary_cases: Common standards proposed via the UN take this and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: Germany calls on UN member states to work towards common safety requirements for the most capable AI models
Providers should be required to test these models before release and report serious safety failures.

themes.label: Inclusive common rules and accountability
themes.definition: Calls for a shared framework, common standards, oversight and accountability for AI with participation of all regions, moving beyond voluntary commitments.
themes.inclusion: Passages on who sets AI rules, accountability, participation of all regions, oversight and common rules.
themes.boundary_cases: Statements that addressing AI is a test for the UN also take AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: We need to ensure that technological progress is guided by a framework that we all have a say in shaping.
we need to ensure accountability, in particular when global peace and security are potentially affected

themes.label: Compute access and avoiding dependencies
themes.definition: Access to compute, data, expertise and infrastructure determines who innovates versus who accepts others' rules; cooperation should build capabilities, not dependencies.
themes.inclusion: Passages on unequal access to AI inputs creating dependency or rule-taking.
themes.exclusion: General digital divide statements without dependency framing (use AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE).
themes.boundary_cases: Concern that AI cements world division if few benefit may take AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE as well.

examples.quote: Cooperation must therefore create capabilities, not new dependencies.

themes.label: AI cementing global division
themes.definition: AI could cement world divisions if only a few benefit, algorithms are partial, or access is limited to rich countries.
themes.inclusion: Passages warning that AI benefits or access are limited to rich countries or few actors.
themes.boundary_cases: Mentions of biased algorithms in this context may also take AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: it can cement the division of the world if only a few benefit from it

themes.label: Rules on generative AI as weapon
themes.definition: Calls for common rules on the possible use of generative AI as a weapon.
themes.inclusion: Passages on weaponization of AI and rules against it.
themes.boundary_cases: Accountability where global peace and security is affected may also count if weapons are implied.

examples.quote: We should also talk about common rules for the possible use of generative artificial intelligence as a weapon.

themes.label: AI as test for UN renewal
themes.definition: Addressing AI together is framed as a test for building a UN for today's world; institutions must catch up with AI; Global Digital Compact engagement.
themes.inclusion: Passages linking AI governance to UN renewal or UN processes like the Global Digital Compact.
themes.exclusion: Governance calls not tied to the UN.
themes.boundary_cases: Statements that institutions must catch up with AI count when the UN context is explicit.

examples.quote: How we address AI together is one of the clearest tests whether we have the strength and the will to build a United Nations for today's world.
AI is not waiting for our institutions to catch up. Our institutions have to catch up with AI.

value.rationale: German passages share a focus on common rules and accountability for AI; 2026 adds concrete frontier-model safety requirements and compute-dependency concerns, while 2023 stresses AI deepening global divisions and rules on AI as a weapon.
